summary: M2 literature lane: two RH-adjacent 2026 arXiv items audited while W76 ran (M5 overlap discipline preserved; W76 cert still pending). ITEM 1 (full line-by-line audit, ~119k chars read end-to-end): arXiv 2610.24612 'Human Exposition of Claude's 2/3 Theorem on the zeros of zeta' (J. Arias de Reyna, Seville; tex date 2026-10-17). Exposes the Claude notes (ref [7]: PDF hosted on www-cdn.anthropic.com, dated 2026-08-10) proving UNCONDITIONALLY N0(T) >= 0.67250 N(T) (simple critical-line zeros; N counts by Re alpha in (T,2T] with multiplicity) and N_d >= 0.83625 N(T) distinct zeros critical-or-not (Prop 9 dyadic form: N0(T) >= (2 - w(psi) + O(loglog T/log T)) N(T)). Previous record: 5/12 = 0.4166 (Pratt-Robles-Zaharescu-Zeindler [23]; the exposition's 'only known 0.4166' claim matches). METHOD (new route, not Levinson): Weil's quadratic form W truncated to the N-point grid {tn = T + nT/N} -> N x N matrix Gnm = (L||f||2^2)^-1 sum_{Re alpha in I'} fhat(alpha - tn) fhat(alpha - tm) with I' = (T-U, 2T+U], U = T^theta, theta in (0,1/2), L = 2piN/T, X = e^L; P = the submatrix over SIMPLE ON-LINE zeros (P is hermitian, real symmetric, and >= 0 - Prop 1); Q := G - P. CORE NEW LEMMA (Theorem 5, rank-trace, P >= 0 hermitian, Q hermitian, Q = Q+ - Q- with Q+ >= 0 and Q- >= 0 by convention, n+(Q) = number of positive eigenvalues of Q): rank(P) >= 4tr(P+Q) - 2tr(P) - 4n+(Q) - ||P+Q||_HS^2. Proof chain VERIFIED line-by-line: (1) expand ||P+Q||^2 = ||P||^2 + ||Q+||^2 + ||Q-||^2 + 2tr(PQ+) - 2tr(PQ-) - 2tr(Q+Q-) with tr(Q+Q-) = 0 (orthogonal positive/negative parts) and tr(PQ+) >= 0 (trace of positive-hermitian product); (2) von Neumann (Mirsky [18]): 0 <= tr(PQ-) <= sum_{j<=n-(Q)} p_j n_j in decreasing eigenvalue order; (3) ||P||^2 + ||Q-||^2 - 2tr(PQ-) >= sum (p_j - n_j)^2 (von Neumann difference inequality for positive matrices); (4) per-term sharpenings, EACH an instance of (x-c)^2 >= 0: (p_j - n_j)^2 >= 2(p_j - n_j) - 1 for j <= rankP, equality n_j^2 = (0 - n_j)^2 for j > rankP; then n^2 >= 4n - 4 both on the tail (n_i^2 -> -4n_i) and, needing n_j >= 0 (holds: Q- is the POSITIVE negative-part operator), 2(p_j - n_j) - 1 >= 2p_j - 4n_j - 1; (5) summation gives 2tr(P) - 4tr(Q-) - rank(P) exactly; (6) ||Q+||^2 = sum q_j^2 >= sum (4q_j - 4) = 4tr(Q+) - 4n+(Q) via (q_j - 2)^2 >= 0; (7) rearrange with tr(Q) = tr(Q+) - tr(Q-). APPLICATION (Theorem 7) VERIFIED with the five Objectives: (a) rank(P) <= N0 + O(UL) [Prop 12]; (b) tr(G) = N + O(U sqrt(T) log T) [Prop 16]; (c) tr(P) <= N0 + O(U sqrt(T) log T) [Prop 17]; (d) n+(Q) <= Nm + Nc + O(UL) [Prop 14]; (e) ||G||_HS^2 = N(w(psi) + O(log L/L)) [Prop 32]. Substitution: N0 + O(UL) >= 4N - 2N0 - 4(Nm + Nc) - w(psi)N - O(NlogL/L) -> 3N0 + 4(Nm + Nc) >= (4 - w)N + O(TlogL) -> N0 >= (4 - w)N - 2(N0 + 2Nm + 2Nc) + O(TlogL) -> N0 >= (2 - w(psi))N + O(TlogL) using N0 + 2Nm + 2Nc <= N. Second claim: subtract N0 + 2Nm + 2Nc <= N from 3N0 + 4(Nm+Nc) >= (4-w)N to get 2(N0 + Nm + Nc) >= (3 - w)N, and Nd = N0 + Nm + 2Nc >= (3 - w)N/2. All arithmetic direction-correct. CONSTANT: w(psi) := (integral psi^2 + double-integral psi(u)psi(v)|u-v| du dv) / (integral psi)^2 over [-1/2,1/2]; min_psi w(psi) = c_MT^{-1} by the Montgomery-Taylor optimization (CITED, not re-derived); 2 - c_MT^{-1} = 0.67250 and (3 - c_MT^{-1})/2 = 0.83625 (internally consistent: c_MT^{-1} = 1.3275 -> c_MT ~ 0.75328; the exposition's 'same as Montgomery [22] and not by coincidence' note is the pair-correlation moment connection via Fourier-analytic duality of w(psi)); best psi is psi_MT(x) = cos(sqrt(2) x). CONDITION: U^2 >> sqrt(log T)/loglog T (Prop 32: needed to absorb the E-matrix ||E||_HS <= e^{L/2}/U^2 into the O(logL/L) relative error; also U sqrt(T) log T = o(N) automatic from theta < 1/2). SUPPORTING ESTIMATES ALL VERIFIED THIS PASS: Prop 16 trace tail (sum_{zeros} (B(Re alpha - tn))^2 over outside-grid terms; two-case split: U log T boundary zeros each O(sqrt T) via sum-vs-integral + Exercise 2, plus interior zeros with distance decay (B(d)^2 + (N/T) int_d^infty B^2) <= C(d^{-4} + (N/T) d^{-3}) and sum d(α)^{-3} << L [Exercise 6(a)] giving total << sqrt T; |N' - N| << U log T) - NOTE FOOTNOTE 11: Alpöge-Furman [1] used U = sqrt T with a bound of ORDER N ('not sufficient'); this exposition's d(alpha)^{-3} tail is the real improvement enabling theta < 1/2; Prop 17 (identical proof, P instead of G); Prop 18 (E = sum over Re alpha NOT in I' of v_alpha (tensor) v_alpha, ||E||_HS <= sum ||v_alpha||^2, each <= e^{L/2} L/d(alpha)^3 [Exercise 8], sum d(alpha)^{-3} <= L/U^2 [Exercise 6(b)]); Prop 20-21 (K_infinity(t,u) = sum_{n in Z} fhat(t-tn) fhat(u-tn) = L fhat_2(t-u) by Poisson [12] with error kernel; |K|, |K_infty| <= L||f||_2^2); Prop 22 (mu bounds: |mu_theta| = (1/2pi)log(|t|/2pi) + O(t^{-2}), |mu_pi| << sqrt X via PNT sum Lambda(n)/sqrt n <= 2 sqrt X [Exercise 9], |mu_sigma| <= sqrt X/(1+|t|)); Prop 23 (||G+E||_HS^2 = ||f||_2^{-4} int_{I x I} (fhat_2)^2 dmu + O(X log L); E1 = O(XL^3logL) via Exercise 10 sum of boundary B-integrals << LlogL; E2 = O(XL^4logL) via sigma(t) <= L min(sqrt L, 1/rho) + Exercise 11); Prop 24 (M(mu_theta, mu_theta) = NL^2 (int psi^2 + O(L^{-1})) via mu_theta(t) = N/T + O(1) on [T,2T], x = t-u change of variables, Plancherel int (fhat_2)^2 = 2pi int f^4, and the Prop 15 ||f||_2^2 = L(int psi)(1 + O(L^{-1})) type identities); Prop 26-28 (M(mu_pi, mu_pi): diagonal D = (T/pi) sum (Lambda(n)^2/n) (f^2 * f^2)(log n) via inverse Fourier; off-diagonal O1 bounded by MONTGOMRY-VAUGHAN HILBERT INEQUALITY [21, CBMS [19] p.140] with |log m - log n| >= 1/2n separation -> |O1| << L (sum n Lambda(n)^2) <= L. X L; O2 << XL via Exercise 9; then partial summation with A(x) = sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n)^2/n = 1/2 (log x)^2 + O(1) [Exercise 9(d)] and |g'| <= 4 (g = f^2*f^2, g' = 2 f^2 * (f f'), int|f'| = 2) -> (T/pi) int_0^L g(y) y dy + O(XL^2) = NL^2 (double-int psi psi |u-v| + O(L^{-1})) via the 1/2 int int psi(u/L) psi(v/L)|u-v| rescaling with boundary-strip error O(L^2)); Prop 29 (M(mu_sigma, mu_sigma) << L); Prop 30 (M(mu_theta, mu_pi) << sqrt X L via integration by parts in u: |int_I m(u) cos(uy)| << L^2/y + Exercise 9); Prop 31 (M(mu_theta, mu_sigma) << sqrt X L^2, M(mu_pi, mu_sigma) << XL); Prop 32 (assembly: M(mu, mu) = NL^2(A + O(L^{-1})), A = int psi^2 + double-int psi psi |u-v|; ||G+E||_HS^2 = N(A/B + O(logL/L)) + O(TlogL) with B = (int psi)^2; change to ||G||: | ||G|| - ||G+E|| | <= ||E||_HS = O(e^{L/2}/U^2), squared-and-divided gives the stated U^2 condition). REMAINING TRUST ITEMS (marked, standard, unproved IN THE PAPER - left as Exercises): Ex 2 (B(x) = min(L, 2/|x|, C/x^2) integral estimates << log L, << L, << min(sqrt L, 1/rho): two integrations by parts + boundary strip of width 1); Ex 6 (sum d(alpha)^{-3} tail bounds via zero counting N(h) << h log h); Ex 8 (||v_alpha||^2 <= e^{L/2} L/d(alpha)^3); Ex 9 (the six PNT partial-summation identities from psi(x) = x + O(x e^{-c sqrt log x})); Ex 10-11 (tail integrals). VERDICT: every displayed non-exercise line of the proof re-derived and direction-checked in this unit; the load-bearing exercise layer is textbook-standard (PNT + integration by parts + sum/integral + zero counting) and the one non-re-derived analytic input (the MT minimization of w(psi)) is CITED to Montgomery-Taylor. The EXPOSITION is a sound presentation of the Claude notes. CORROBORATION: ref [15] Y. Lamzouri 'A new proof that more than 2/3 of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line' arXiv:2609.02882 (2026) - an independent HUMAN proof of the same >2/3 result exists; ref [1] Alpöge-Furman 2608.13637 (v2) 'More than two thirds ... simple and on the critical line' is the nearest prior art; the author states in s1.1 that [1] 'doesn't work as written' and, of its claimed Lean verification, asks 'if they say Lean has verified the proof, how is it possible that this paper includes false statements that invalidate the proof?' - UNVERIFIED CLAIM about AF's Lean status, recorded as such (we did not audit AF's Lean in this unit); s1.2 coins the 'AI claims' category (between conjecture and theorem until a mathematician validates) and says it took him a month to be convinced of the notes.
